title: Alibaba Cloud opens Malaysia's first global public cloud data centre
description: Alibaba Cloud began operating a data centre in Kuala Lumpur, billed as the first global public cloud platform in Malaysia. It linked to Alibaba's Hong Kong and Singapore sites.
significance: A Chinese hyperscaler planted the first flag, years before the US cloud giants arrived.

title: Singapore pauses new data centre approvals
description: Singapore imposed an informal moratorium on new data centres while it reviewed the sector's energy and land use.
significance: Pushed new capacity across the causeway and seeded Johor's boom.

title: MyDIGITAL digital economy blueprint launched
description: The government launched MyDIGITAL, the Malaysia Digital Economy Blueprint, setting a cloud-first direction for the public sector.
significance: Set the policy frame that later incentives for data centres plugged into.

title: Microsoft plans first Malaysian datacenter region
description: Microsoft announced its first datacenter region in Greater Kuala Lumpur under the Bersama Malaysia initiative. Malaysian officials put the initiative at about US$1 billion; Microsoft's own release gives no dollar figure.
significance: First US hyperscaler commitment, signalling Malaysia as a cloud destination rather than a Singapore spillover.
source_name: EdgeProp (The Edge group); Microsoft press release 19 Apr 2021

title: DESAC tax incentive for data centres opens (Budget 2022)
description: Under Budget 2022, MIDA began accepting DESAC applications. Data centres could claim a 100% investment tax allowance on capital spending for up to ten years.
significance: The core fiscal carrot of the boom; 25 MD-status data centre projects had received DESAC incentives by June 2025.

title: Singapore lifts moratorium under selective regime
description: Singapore ended its three-year pause and said it would admit new data centres selectively through a pilot call for applications with strict efficiency rules.
significance: Singapore stayed capacity constrained, so most regional growth continued to flow to Johor.

title: Google Cloud announces plans for a Malaysia cloud region
description: Google Cloud said it would build new cloud regions in Malaysia, Thailand and New Zealand. A Malaysia-specific launch event followed on 12 August 2022.
significance: Brought a second US hyperscaler into the Malaysian pipeline just as Singapore reopened selectively.

title: US imposes sweeping chip export controls on China
description: The US Commerce Department restricted exports of advanced computing chips and chipmaking tools to China.
actor: US Bureau of Industry and Security
significance: Created the incentive for Chinese firms to seek compute in third countries such as Malaysia.

title: AWS commits US$6 billion to a Malaysian cloud region through 2037
description: Amazon Web Services said it would launch an infrastructure region in Malaysia and invest about RM25.5 billion (US$6 billion) by 2037. PM Anwar Ibrahim announced it at AWS Cloud Day.
significance: The largest single cloud pledge to that point and an early win for the new Anwar government.

title: Singapore awards 80 MW in pilot data centre call
description: Singapore provisionally awarded about 80 MW to AirTrunk-ByteDance, Equinix, GDS and Microsoft.
significance: A tiny allocation next to Johor's gigawatt pipeline, underlining Singapore's scarcity.

title: TNB launches Green Lane Pathway for data centres
description: TNB launched a fast-track that cut grid connection for high-voltage data centres from 36-48 months to about 12, with a one-stop centre. It signed supply deals with Yondr, AirTrunk, SIPP and GDS.
significance: Speed to power became Malaysia's main edge over Singapore and turned interest into signed load.

title: US tightens AI chip export rules
description: BIS updated its 2022 rules, adding a performance density threshold and extending licence needs to arms-embargoed countries and to firms headquartered in them.
actor: US Bureau of Industry and Security
significance: Closed loopholes and raised the stakes of chips leaking to China via Southeast Asia.

title: YTL Power and Nvidia announce US$4.3 billion AI data centre project
description: After Jensen Huang met PM Anwar, YTL Power said it would partner Nvidia on AI cloud and supercomputing at its planned 500 MW YTL Green Data Centre Park in Kulai, Johor.
significance: Marked the turn from cloud storage to AI compute and tied Malaysia directly to Nvidia's supply chain.

title: Microsoft raises Malaysia commitment to US$2.2 billion
description: Satya Nadella announced US$2.2 billion over four years for cloud and AI infrastructure, AI skilling and an AI centre of excellence in Malaysia.
significance: Kicked off a run of about US$17 billion in hyperscaler pledges in roughly five months of 2024.

title: Google pledges US$2 billion for first Malaysian data centre
description: Google announced US$2 billion for its first Malaysian data centre and cloud region at Elmina Business Park, Selangor. Ground was broken on 1 October 2024.
significance: Confirmed that every major US cloud provider was now building physically in Malaysia.

title: ByteDance plans RM10 billion AI hub in Malaysia
description: Trade minister Tengku Zafrul said ByteDance planned to invest RM10 billion (about US$2.1 billion) to make Malaysia a regional AI hub.
significance: Showed Chinese tech firms using Malaysia as an offshore compute base as US chip controls tightened.

title: AirTrunk opens 150 MW JHB1 campus in Johor Bahru
description: Australian operator AirTrunk opened JHB1, a hyperscale campus planned for 150 MW, with just over 50 MW in its first phases.
significance: Johor's hyperscale build-out shifted from announcements to operating capacity.

title: AWS launches Malaysia region, raises plan to US$6.2 billion
description: AWS launched its Asia Pacific (Malaysia) Region and said it would invest about RM29.2 billion (US$6.2 billion) through 2038.
significance: First of the new US hyperscale regions to go live in Malaysia.

title: CRESS green power scheme opens to corporate buyers
description: The Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme let firms such as data centres buy renewable power directly from developers over TNB's grid, paying a system access charge.
actor: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation
significance: Gave hyperscalers with net-zero pledges a path to green power in a coal and gas heavy grid.

title: Oracle to invest over US$6.5 billion in a Malaysian cloud region
description: Oracle announced plans to invest more than US$6.5 billion to open a public cloud region in Malaysia.
significance: Capped the 2024 wave of US hyperscaler commitments.

title: Bridge Data Centres signs 400 MW power deal with TNB
description: Bridge Data Centres signed agreements with TNB covering 400 MW for its MY07 campus in Ulu Tiram, Johor, becoming the first partner under the CRESS green power scheme.
actor: Bridge Data Centres; Tenaga Nasional Berhad
significance: Shows the scale of single-campus power demand and the link between data centres and green power access.

title: GDS International becomes independent DayOne
description: GDS's overseas unit, with major Johor campuses, rebranded as DayOne after raising about US$1.9 billion in Series A and B equity to support up to 1 GW of capacity.
significance: A China-origin operator restructured as Singapore-based, illustrating how Johor capacity sits across US-China lines.

title: Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone agreement signed
description: Malaysia and Singapore signed the JS-SEZ agreement during PM Lawrence Wong's visit, targeting 50 projects and 20,000 skilled jobs in five years.
significance: Formalised Johor as Singapore's hinterland, including for data centres priced out of Singapore.

title: US AI Diffusion Rule places Malaysia in Tier 2
description: BIS issued the AI Diffusion framework, capping advanced chip exports to most countries. Malaysia was not among the Tier 1 allies and faced compute caps.
actor: US Bureau of Industry and Security
significance: Threatened the GPU supply that Malaysia's AI data centre pipeline depended on.

title: Water regulator approved under 18% of data centre requests
description: SPAN said 101 data centres sought 808 million litres a day in 2024 but only 142 million were approved, citing insufficient supply.
significance: First hard data showing water, not just power, as a binding constraint.

title: Singapore charges three in server fraud linked to Nvidia chips
description: Singapore charged three men with fraud over servers likely containing Nvidia chips. Minister Shanmugam later said the servers were shipped on to Malaysia, which may not have been the final destination.
significance: Put Malaysia at the centre of US concerns about AI chip diversion to China.

title: US rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule
description: Commerce rescinded the rule before its 15 May compliance date and issued new guidance on chip diversion and Huawei Ascend chips.
actor: US Bureau of Industry and Security
significance: Removed the Tier 2 cap but shifted pressure onto transit countries to police diversion.

title: Malaysia probes Chinese firm's use of Nvidia servers
description: After a WSJ report that Chinese engineers flew data to Malaysia to train AI on rented Nvidia servers, MITI said it was checking whether any local law was broken.
significance: Showed Malaysian data centres being used to route around US controls without moving chips to China.

title: New tariff structure raises data centre power costs
description: A new voltage-based tariff took effect, with most large data centres expected in the ultra-high-voltage band. Officials estimated costs rising 10% to 14% before surcharges.
significance: Ended the era of cheap power as a selling point and began pricing grid strain into the business case.

title: Malaysia requires permits for US-origin AI chip exports
description: MITI ruled that all exports, transshipments and transit of US-origin high-performance AI chips need a Strategic Trade Permit, with 30 days' notice.
significance: Malaysia began enforcing US chip rules itself to protect its access to GPUs.

title: MIDA made single entry point for data centre approvals
description: The Data Centre Task Force named MIDA the focal point for all new and expanded data centre applications and promised a sustainable data centre framework by October 2025.
significance: Centralised gatekeeping, the tool later used to screen projects on power and water.

title: System access charge cut for CRESS green power
description: The energy ministry cut the CRESS system access charge for firm supply from 25 to 20 sen/kWh and for non-firm supply from 45 to 40 sen/kWh. Charges were revised again in October 2026.
actor: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation
significance: Made direct green power purchases more viable for data centres facing higher grid tariffs.

title: US and Malaysia sign reciprocal trade agreement
description: Trump and Anwar signed a trade deal holding the US tariff at 19%. Malaysia committed to export control cooperation and about US$150 billion of purchases including chips and data centre equipment.
significance: Tied Malaysia's data centre equipment and export controls to the US trade relationship.

title: Data centres draw 603 MW against 1,276 MW declared
description: MITI told Parliament 143 data centre projects worth RM144.4 billion were approved from 2021 to June 2025, while actual use was 603 MW, about 47% of declared demand.
significance: The gap between booked and used capacity drove the later 85% utilisation rule.

title: Johor stops approving water-intensive Tier 1 and 2 data centres
description: Johor said it would no longer approve Tier 1 and Tier 2 data centres, which it said can use up to 50 million litres of water a day, about 200 times higher-tier sites.
significance: The first hard brake on the boom came from a state government over water, not power.

title: Rules require data centres to use 85% of declared power
description: Under supply agreements, data centres must reach 85% of declared maximum demand or pay RM8.50 per kW of shortfall in the first four years. New projects also need Data Centre Task Force approval.
significance: Targets phantom demand, where grid capacity is booked but not used, protecting other consumers.

title: First public protest against a data centre in Malaysia
description: About 50 residents protested at a data centre construction site in Gelang Patah, Johor, over dust, health and possible water supply impacts.
significance: Local opposition joined grid and water limits as a political constraint on the boom.

title: Anwar confirms halt on approvals for non-AI data centres
description: PM Anwar told Parliament the government had stopped approving data centres not linked to AI, citing sharp rises in energy and water use.
significance: Shift from courting all data centres to rationing grid and water for AI workloads only.

title: Customs seizes 72 AI servers at KLIA
description: Customs seized 72 servers with advanced AI chips worth RM52.9 million that were declared as ordinary parts and bound for re-export without a permit.
significance: First large enforcement under the 2025 permit rule, showing Malaysia policing chip transit.

title: Data centres forecast to use 31% of power by 2035
description: The energy ministry told Parliament data centres use about 7% of electricity in 2026 (10,544 GWh), projected to reach 31% (73,274 GWh) by 2035.
actor: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation
significance: Puts the energy security stakes in one number: nearly a third of national demand.

title: TNB holds supply deals for 59 data centres totalling 8.3 GW
description: Per RHB Research after meeting TNB management, 59 data centre projects have supply agreements for 8.3 GW, 36 of them completed, all on five-year take-or-pay terms.
significance: Contracted load equals roughly 39% of projected 2026 Peninsular peak demand (21.3 GW), though actual draw is far lower.

title: Approvals now hinge on surplus power and water, says MITI
description: Deputy minister Sim Tze Tzin told Parliament the Data Centre Task Force checks power and water capacity first, and water must go to residents before data centres.
significance: Made resource availability an explicit federal test for every new project.

title: Singapore awards 200 MW in second data centre call
description: Singapore gave 50 MW each to Digital Realty, Equinix, Keppel Data Centres and ST Telemedia from 20 proposals.
significance: Singapore is reopening slowly, but at a scale still far below Johor's pipeline.

title: Google unveils US$15 billion Malaysia data centre expansion
description: Google said it will invest US$15 billion over 2027 to 2028 in new campuses in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan and add over 1 GW of clean energy capacity to the grid.
significance: The largest single commitment yet, arriving under the new rule that projects must prove power and water supply.

title: Data centres draw 1,374 MW of 2,346 MW contracted
description: The energy ministry said that as of August 2026 data centres drew 1,374 MW, 58.6% of contracted capacity, and would reach 21% of Peninsular demand by 2030. It requires 10-year load plans for new connections.
actor: Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation
significance: Actual load more than doubled in about 14 months from 603 MW, while the phantom-demand gap persists.
